# About this report {#about}

This report summarises the PhIP-seq antibody repertoire analysis of
**`r book$project`**, produced by the `phipflow` pipeline. Figures and tables
are read from the phipflow results (`r book$results_dir`) when the book is
rendered; the results are linked, not copied.

```{r, results='asis'}
cat(cohort_numbers(book))
```

```{r, results='asis'}
cat(fastqc_tile(book))
```

## Comparisons

PERMANOVA R² is the share of repertoire variance explained by the grouping.
DELTA counts are features tested, features passing the significance filter and
features shown in this report (see [DELTA overview](#delta-overview)).

```{r, results='asis'}
cat(comparison_table(book))
```

## Report structure

- **Cohort and demographics**: age and sex for the cohort and per comparison,
  with tests where the groups are different people. Present when the metadata
  has age or sex.
- **General analyses**: per comparison, enrichment counts, alpha diversity,
  beta diversity (PCoA, CAP, PERMANOVA, dispersion, t-SNE) and the POP
  prevalence plots.
- **Repertoire stability**: within- versus between-individual similarity, for
  paired (longitudinal) comparisons only.
- **DELTA overview**: the selected DELTA features of every comparison, each
  linking to its detail page.
- **DELTA features**: per feature, its statistics and the scatter, Δ and ECDF
  plots.

Chapters are the `.Rmd` files of the book directory. Edit them, add your own,
or switch one off by renaming it with a leading `_` (see `README.md` in the
book directory).

## What each analysis shows

### Enrichment counts
How many peptides are called enriched per sample, by group. Large systematic
shifts can be biology, but can equally be batch or sequencing-depth effects.

### Alpha diversity
Within-sample repertoire richness. Sensitive to immune exposure history, but
also to technical factors; read it alongside age and sex.

### Beta diversity
Between-sample differences on a Kulczynski distance matrix, with PCoA, CAP,
PERMANOVA and a dispersion test.

- If **PERMANOVA is significant but dispersion also differs**, the separation
  may come from unequal variability rather than a consistent shift.
- **R² matters as much as the p-value**: a small p-value on a very small R²
  is a consistent but minor shift.
- **t-SNE is for visualisation only**; use the distance-based tests for
  inference.

### POP framework
Prevalence comparisons at peptide level and across taxonomic ranks. Each point
is a feature; the axes give its prevalence in the two groups, so the distance
from the diagonal shows the size of the difference.

### DELTA framework
A permutation test for prevalence shifts of taxa and proteins
(`r paste(unique(stats::na.omit(vapply(book$comparisons, delta_permutations, 1L))), collapse = " / ")`
permutations per feature). A feature passes when its effective number of
peptides m<sub>eff</sub> &gt; `r book$delta$min_m_eff` and `p_perm` &lt; 0.05.

- **`p_perm`** is the raw permutation p-value, **not corrected** for the
  thousands of features tested per comparison: expect false positives and
  treat the feature lists as hypothesis-generating.
- **Direction** tells which group has the higher prevalence; **`max_delta`** is
  the largest peptide-level prevalence difference.
- This report shows, per rank and direction, the `r book$delta$top_n`
  passing features with the highest phipflow **weighted score**
  (|T_obs_stand| and max_delta, each scaled to 0-1 within the rank, multiplied),
  plus any features added by hand in `report_config.yml`.

### Similarity (paired comparisons only)
Within-subject versus between-subject Kulczynski similarity: how stable a
person's repertoire is over time compared with how different people are from
each other.
